correctness.rationale: Exact expansion of two L4 quartics gives uniform arithmetic-mean coefficients F/2 and B. Completing the exact L2-square defect yields F+1/sqrt2=r²/(2sqrt2), with |B-9/16|<=4r from independent identities for D and C+E. This proves the uniform O(tau³) lower bound after a quadratic completion. The two-disjoint-support unit pair gives identical output L4 norms and common fourth-power polynomial 1-sqrt2 tau+3tau²+sqrt2 tau³+tau⁴, hence an outer-exponent-independent matching upper bound. Near-optimizers satisfy r=O(tau) by the same uncompleted inequality. Ratio-root equality conditions and their y⁴ mass fractions are algebraically reconstructed. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.
